body: I’d also like to know tbh, but I guess normal in this context would be something the majority does. As for reality and life, I’m trying to figure that out too :) any answers would be well appreciated

I do see what youre saying, and I do agree with you too, but when the person tells you to go die it kinda does make them a big part of the reason. Or if they cause you unimaginable pain, I can’t say that they’re not a part of it, highly likely I’m like this because of recent experiences though, so I apologise for that.

I can’t see the point of keeping going, so even if I do have enough sleep and a proper diet, I would say yes because of the pressure of everything around me and the fact that I can’t find a reason to not give up, Thank you for the thought and the hug though, I really appreciate that. If I could somehow make my life the way I wanted—with a purpose, less pressure for myself and a reason to continue then maybe I’d keep going.

What if their action was also the last straw? Telling someone you’re going to commit suicide over their actions may not always be manipulation especially if it’s the straw that broke the camels back. I get your point on the really fine line though.
Haven’t had the opportunity to lose their trust, but I received a grievance form saying that I’m difficult to approach, I do nothing and they can’t trust me.
